options.how: Phones or tablets are the controllers: players join from their own devices, so 1 to 100 people can play with no extra pads.
Each of four players holds an N64 controller; minigames after every board turn test stick and button reflexes.

sources.note: The Jackbox Party Pack: phones or tablets are your controllers, 1 to 100 players
Mario Party: Nintendo 64 controller input, minigames after each turn test reflexes

options.how: Players type punchlines to prompts on their phones or tablets, used as controllers, then vote on the funniest.
Each microgame tells players to hold the Wii Remote in a different Form and act it out, passing the remote around.

sources.note: Use Your Words: players use their phones or tablets as controllers to answer prompts
WarioWare: Smooth Moves: built around the Wii Remote and its Forms

options.how: One player uses the Wii U GamePad's private second screen to chase or hide from four Wii Remote players (Mario Chase).
1 to 8 players each use a controller on one shared screen for board turns and minigames, locally or online.

sources.note: Nintendo Land: GamePad player pursues or is pursued by the other players
Pummel Party: 1 to 8 players compete on the same screen, controller support

options.how: Every player runs the game on their own phone or tablet and shouts instructions across the room; there is no shared screen.
Players on controllers place traps and race in one shared level on a single screen, locally or online.

sources.note: Spaceteam: a cooperative shouting game for phones and tablets
Ultimate Chicken Horse: party platformer, local and online play, controller support

options.how: Players write answers privately on their phones, then vote; an audience of thousands can join and vote from their devices.
Each player holds a Joy-Con or Pro Controller for board turns and 100 classic minigames on the TV.

sources.note: Quiplash: your phones or tablets are your controllers, plus an audience
Mario Party Superstars: Joy-Con and Pro Controller input, 100 minigames

options.how: Players sketch prompts on their phone touch screens, then type fake titles for each other's drawings.
2 to 8 players on controllers share one screen; one hit eliminates, so reflexes on a pad decide rounds.

sources.note: Drawful 2: phones or tablets are your controllers, game of terrible drawings
Duck Game: 2 to 8 local players, one hit and you're roasted

options.how: Each player joins a local WiFi or online lobby from their own phone or PC and sees only their own view; no shared TV.
2 to 4 players brawl on one screen with controllers in local play, or online; there is no single player mode.

sources.note: Among Us: 4-15 players online or via local WiFi, cross-play with Android and iOS
Stick Fight: The Game: 2 to 4 players local or online, controller support

options.how: In Bowser Party one player controls Bowser on the Wii U GamePad's second screen against up to four Wii Remote players.
Everyone uses a controller and watches the same screen; items and minigames are symmetric for all players.

sources.note: Mario Party 10: Bowser Party, one player controls Bowser using the GamePad
Pummel Party: local same-screen play, controller support

options.how: Crewmates do tasks while hidden Impostors kill; players discuss and vote to eject suspects, so sides win or lose.
Up to four chefs share one shifting kitchen, throwing ingredients and crossing teleporters to fill orders together.

sources.note: Among Us: Impostors among the Crew, social deduction
Overcooked! 2: chaotic co-op cooking, teleporters and moving platforms

options.how: Players race to collect Stars and Coins on classic boards, winning extra Coins in minigames; one player wins.
Couch co-op movers carry physics-driven furniture to the truck together on shared moving jobs.

sources.note: Mario Party Superstars: boards and 100 minigames from past Mario Party games
Moving Out: physics-based moving simulator built for couch co-op

options.how: Classic Battle Mode drops players into a maze arena to trap and bomb each other, locally or online.
1 to 4 players share one ship, running between turrets, lasers, shields and thrusters; survival needs teamwork.

sources.note: Super Bomberman R: classic Battle Mode, local and online
Lovers in a Dangerous Spacetime: co-op crew mans turrets, shields and thrusters

options.how: 2 to 8 ducks blast each other with shotguns, net guns and saxophones; one hit and you are out of the round.
One player sees the bomb, the Experts hold the manual; everyone must talk it out fast to defuse it together.

sources.note: Duck Game: battle with shotguns and odd weapons, one hit and you're roasted
Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes: Experts with the manual guide the defuser

options.how: A battle royale of obstacle rounds: players dive and dodge, and rounds eliminate until one wins.
Teammates gather resources and craft track ahead of a moving train; let it derail and everyone loses.

sources.note: Fall Guys: party battle royale, dive and dodge your way to victory
Unrailed!: co-op railroad construction, keep the train from derailing

options.how: Players place traps in a level they all build, then race it; you score only if you finish and friends do not.
Up to four players build and run one restaurant, placing appliances, cooking and serving between shifts.

sources.note: Ultimate Chicken Horse: build the level, place traps, score if you make it and friends don't
PlateUp!: up to four players build and run a restaurant together

options.how: 2 to 4 stick figures brawl with physics-based combat across 100 interactive levels, local or online.
Up to 8 wobbly physics characters solve physics puzzle levels together, online or in local co-op.

sources.note: Stick Fight: The Game: physics-based fighting for 2 to 4 players
Human: Fall Flat: physics puzzle co-op with up to 8 players online

options.how: Players hinder each other in the race for Stars; minigames range from free-for-alls to 1-vs-3 for Coins.
Four heroes fight endless monster hordes through dungeons together in classic 4-player co-op.

sources.note: Mario Party: players hinder others in the quest for Stars, free-for-all and 1-vs-3 minigames
Gauntlet Slayer Edition: classic 4-player co-op dungeon brawler

options.how: Players join at jackbox.tv on their phones with a room code and draw or type there, while the host screen runs the game.
Everyone holds Joy-Con: board turns and minigames, including motion ones like Rhythm Kitchen, use the controller in hand.

sources.note: The Jackbox Party Pack 10: use phones as controllers, join at jackbox.tv with the room code
The Jackbox Party Pack 10: drawing battles in Tee K.O. 3, 3 to 8 players
Super Mario Party Jamboree: play using Joy-Con controllers, motion minigames like Rhythm Kitchen

options.how: Team games for groups of 2 to 100: big crowds join on their own smart devices, while Joy-Con mode caps at 8 players.
Each player grips a Joy-Con and shakes, punches and poses through 200+ microgames lasting seconds.

sources.note: Everybody 1-2-Switch!: up to 100 players in smart device mode, up to 8 in Joy-Con mode
WarioWare: Move It!: shake, punch and dance with Joy-Con through 200+ microgames; Party Mode one Joy-Con each

options.how: Roll dice to race around the board for Stars; minigame wins earn coins to buy Stars, and the most Stars at the end wins.
2 to 8 players clear 2D action puzzles that only open up when everyone works together.

sources.note: Super Mario Party Jamboree: roll dice to race for Stars, win minigames for coins, most Stars wins
Pico Park 2: co-op action-puzzle for 2 to 8 players where working together is key
